math/aggregate#

One-pass aggregates over Iterating values.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let smallest is int = Extremes(numbers).minimum();
let largest is int = Extremes([3, 9, 4]).maximum();
let total is float = Numbers(measurements).accurate_sum();
let length is float = Numbers(coordinates).hypotenuse();
let gap is float = Vectors(left: first, right: second).distance();

Description#

One-pass aggregates over Iterating values. Plain arrays are Iterating, so no wrapper object is needed:

Extremes uses intrinsic Comparing<T> and throws EmptySequence for an empty source. sum, accurate_sum and dot return 0.0 for empty input; product returns 1.0; hypotenuse returns 0.0.

sum is a plain left fold. accurate_sum uses Neumaier compensation and is the default when cancellation accuracy matters. hypotenuse and distance use a scaled sum of squares, avoiding direct x*x overflow and underflow. dot traverses both inputs once and throws UnequalSizes when only one ends; distance checks the sizes before reading either value.
